snapshots.captured_representation: Australian Greens announced on 7 September 2026 that Vanessa Bleyer joined the federal team after Pete Whish-Wilson's departure; Bleyer took Agriculture, Science/Industry/Innovation, Tourism and Healthy Oceans portfolios; David Shoebridge became spokesperson for Digital Rights and AI.

snapshots.source_name: Liberal Party of Australia — Coalition illicit tobacco policy
snapshots.captured_representation: The Liberal Party published a Coalition policy on 3 September 2026 proposing an 80% cut to tobacco excise, legalisation/regulation/taxation of vapes and nicotine pouches for adults, and a $200 million nationwide law-enforcement surge against illicit tobacco.
snapshots.notes: Primary party source. Joint Coalition policy is attached to Liberal and Nationals state events without collapsing the parties into one team.

snapshots.source_name: Pauline Hanson's One Nation — tobacco policy
snapshots.captured_representation: One Nation published a tobacco policy on 1 September 2026 proposing a 75% cut to tobacco excise, a three-year pause in indexation, and tougher action against organised crime and illicit tobacco.
snapshots.notes: Primary party source. Underlying numerical claims in the release are not independently promoted to verified facts by this snapshot.

snapshots.captured_representation: Australian Labor Party published on 21 August 2026 that the 100th residential housing development had received approval under the EPBC Act and stated that more than 80,000 new homes had been given the green light under national environmental law under the government to date.
snapshots.notes: Primary party/government-position source. The snapshot verifies the published position; numerical claims remain attributed to the release unless separately corroborated.

Changes to electoral law The Electoral Amendment Act 2026 made some changes to the Electoral Act 2002, the law state elections are run under. The full list of changes is on our Electoral Act amendments page. Some key differences are: the electoral roll closes at 8 pm the day the writ of an election is issued, 1 week earlier than other elections. This year the roll will close at 8 pm on Tuesday 3 November , Melbourne Cup Day. there are fewer days for candidates to nominate. If you're an independent candidate, make sure you're prepared before nominations open on Wednesday 4 November. the early voting period is shorter. This year early voting will be available from Wednesday 18 to Friday 27 November. Changes we have made This year we've made some changes we think will make it easier for all Victorians to actively participate in their democracy. Low sensory voting – there'll be a low-sensory mobile voting session in every district on Tuesday 17 November between 10am and 4pm. We'll share more information about this session later this year. Early voting centres – all early voting centres will also be election day voting centres. This will make it easier to find a voting centre location that works for you. EasyVote guide – we're mailing a printed version of our EasyVote guide to all households. This pamphlet will have all the key information about when, where, and how to vote correctly. Prepare for November Become a candidate Candidate nominations: open at 9 am Wednesday 4 November close at 12 noon on Monday 9 November for all candidates . There is a shorter nomination period this year. If you’re an independent candidate, make sure you’re prepared before nominations open. Independent candidates must nominate in person at the election office of the electorate they’re nominating in. For district (lower house) independent candidates, this will be the district election office. For region (upper house) independent candidates this will be any district election office within your region. From Wednesday 14 October, Candidate Helper will have: nomination forms election office locations opening hours contact information Registered political parties must lodge the nomination forms for their endorsed candidates directly with us. More information Become a state election candidate Know your electorate Victoria is made up of 88 districts and 8 regions. The 88 districts make up Victoria’s lower house of Parliament, the Legislative Assembly. Each district is represented by one Member of Parliament (MP for short). The 8 regions make up Victoria’s upper house of Parliament, the Legislative Council. Each region is represented by 5 Members of Parliament. If you’ve moved house since the 2022 state election, you might be voting in a new electorate. If you do move house, it’s your responsibility to keep your enrolment up to date . Why this is important When candidates nominate for an election, they nominate for either one district or one region. When you go to vote, you’ll be given ballot papers for the district and region you’re enrolled in. If you want to find out more about the candidates who want your vote, you need to know which electorate you’re enrolled in. Knowing your electorate also helps you plan where you go to vote, if you want to vote in person. If you do vote in person, knowing which electorate you’re enrolled in can make it faster for you at the voting centre. More information What are electoral boundaries? There are also jobs in the months before and after election day. snapshots.captured_representation: Hansard - Parliament of Victoria Skip to content Parliamentary activity Hansard Hansard is the official report of the proceedings of the Parliament of Victoria from 1866 to the present day. It is a comprehensive record of the debates that shape legislation and the speeches that inform policymaking in Victoria. Proceedings from 1856 to 1866 were reported in the Argus newspaper. Hansard captures key issues affecting Victorians, the government’s priorities, the views and policies of opposition parties and concerns individuals or groups have raised with their local member. Hansard is published progressively on sitting days. You can find a member’s speech on Browse Hansard within 3 hours. A proof version of the full day’s proceedings is published 4 hours after the sitting day has finished. A final version of Hansard is available five working days later. Browse Hansard and Argus records by day or week (1851–present) Search Hansard by keyword (1991–present) Editorial policy Hansard’s publishing team corrects for grammar and obvious factual errors. Hansard is substantially verbatim and some parliamentary formalities are shown in summarised form – for example, divisions (votes) and procedural motions. Members can review Hansard and suggest corrections to obvious errors, such as incorrect dates, names or figures, but they cannot ask for changes that alter the meaning of their speech. Interjections The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly and President of the Legislative Council give members the call – their turn to speak. Interjections are not usually recorded in Hansard unless they are responded to and relate directly to the matter at hand. Incorporated material and quotes Some parts of the Hansard report are incorporated, which means the words were not spoken in the chamber. This material is clearly indicated in Hansard. Similarly, when members quote at length from articles, letters or emails, this material will be indented. Hansard requires members to provide the sources of their quotes. Committees While the Hansard publishing team produces parliamentary committee transcripts, committees are responsible for publishing the transcripts. These can be found on the committees pages on the Parliament of Victoria website. More about committees Argus reports From 1851 to 1856, Victoria had only one legislative body, the Legislative Council, which held its proceedings at St Patrick’s Hall in Bourke Street, Melbourne. Proceedings of the Council were reported in the Argus newspaper. Argus editorials concerning the Legislative Council have been included with reports of the proceedings. The Argus reports can be found in Browse Hansard . There are different ways to search Hansard depending on what you are looking for. If you know the specific date, view Hansard by day on the Hansard search page. Update : The Hansard Search will now return refined results for the 41st and 42nd Parliament (2021-current day). This is part of an ongoing project to migrate past Hansards into a modern advanced search platform. Please report any issues to itservicedesk@parliament.wa.gov.au . Support How to search Hansard 2021 - current (41st and 42nd Parliaments) Hansard search Note: The 41st Parliament (2021-2024) is now included in these search results. Use keyword search for general words or phrases. Use quotation marks to search for an exact phrase. Use filters to refine your search. Parliament: select the four-year term of Parliament House: Legislative Council or Legislative Assembly Date range Member: Search by the member who spoke on a particular topic. Multiple members may be selected by pressing SHIFT when selecting a member from the dropdown list Bill: Find all search results on a particular bill Proceeding: Find all search results on a parliamentary proceeding, e.g. second reading, grievance, petition. Multiple proceedings may be selected by pressing SHIFT when selecting a proceeding from the dropdown list Select ‘Apply filter’ to run your search. Search results The default display order for search results is newest to oldest. Results can be further refined by selecting the metadata in the left-hand side of the screen. Electorate House Members Ministry Proceeding Subproceeding Parliament. Clicking ‘Download PDF’ in the top right-hand corner will download a print-ready version of the proceeding. Clicking 'Daily PDF' will download the full day Hansard currently available. Note, this document is generated from the online version which can be subject to further correction. See Hansard Publication below. Boolean operators The Hansard search requires all words in your query to appear in the result. So, if you search for maternity hospital , you'll only get results that contain both words. The Boolean operators AND, OR, and NOT only work as operators when your search terms are wrapped in double quotes. Without quotes, they're treated as ordinary search words. Bill: Find all search results on a particular bill Committees: Search for references to standing committees in Parliament. Dates: Select a custom date search by Year Date Date range. Proceeding: Find all search results on a parliamentary proceeding, e.g. second reading, grievance, petition. Page no.: Search for a particular page in the final Hansard. Results per page: the default is 100 Sort order: Select the order in which you want your results displayed Search results Click on the date on the left side to bring up the PDF of that proceeding. Click on the PDF symbol on the right to access the Hansard of the entire day. Results can be further refined by adding more filters to the advanced search on the results page. Update: Hansard Search filters now apply to speeches for the 41st and 42nd Parliament (2021-current day). The Refined Hansard search (2000 - 2024) will remain available during this transition. Historical Hansard 1870 to July 2000 Hansard search Hansards between 1870 to 2000 have been scanned from the printed bound volumes and search results may not always be reliable. Use keyword search for general words or phrases. Use quotation marks to search for an exact phrase. Use filters to refine your search. Parliament: select the four-year term of Parliament House: Legislative Council or Legislative Assembly Date range Note : Filters for bills, proceedings and members will not work for Hansards prior to 2021. Select ‘Apply filter’ to run your search. Search results The default display order for search results is newest to oldest. The Hansard indexes provide information about member speeches and subjects, and can be used to assist your search. Find the indexes here: Hansard Indexes . For those who were familiar with the previous method of searching the 1870-2000 Hansards, the search is available here Frequently asked questions How can I find all the speeches made by a particular member? You can find all of a current member’s speeches in their member’s page on the Parliament website, by navigating to Current Members and searching or browsing for the member. Member speeches are separated into two categories: Speeches prior to 2021, returning refined Hansard search (2000 - 2024) results Speeches from 2021 onwards, returning results using the current Hansard Search . To search for speeches by former members, use the Refined Hansard search (2000-2024) , select the Member filter, and press Search. For members who served prior to 2000, use the Historical Search or the Hansard Search to free text search their name and/or topic. How can I read what was said on a bill? The Bills section of the public website displays a history on each bill page, a copy of the bill, the explanatory memorandum and a link to second reading speeches. To find further debates in the Hansard search, select the relevant bill from the dropdown list and select Search. How can I find the broadcast for a particular speech? Videos of parliamentary debates from April 2021 are available on our Video Archives . Why are there multiple Hansard searches? We are progressively upgrading the Hansard search to provide a more modern, consistent and powerful way to search parliamentary records. Hansard is the official record of parliamentary debates and a historically significant resource, and it is important that users can easily and reliably find information within Hansard. Because historical Hansard records have been created and stored in different formats over many years, upgrading the search is a complex process. Each Parliament must be carefully reviewed and prepared before it can be added to the new system. During this project, multiple search tools will remain available. How to find committee transcripts Committee transcripts are published in the committees section of the public website, for both current and past committees. When is Hansard available? Hansard is published progressively throughout the sitting day, with the full version generally appearing online within three hours of the house rising. This is a draft version, with the final, corrected Hansard appearing two to three days after the sitting. Finalised Hansard is available: for Tuesday by <TIME> Friday for Wednesday by <TIME> Monday following a sitting week for Thursday by <TIME> Tuesday following a sitting week. Please note: Public holidays may result in delays. Although we encourage the use of the Hansard record, the draft should not be quoted as it may be subject to further correction. Any changes made to the draft Hansard will be automatically reflected online. There are different ways to search Hansard depending on what you are looking for. If you know the specific date, view Hansard by day on the Hansard search page. Update : The Hansard Search will now return refined results for the 41st and 42nd Parliament (2021-current day). This is part of an ongoing project to migrate past Hansards into a modern advanced search platform. Please report any issues to itservicedesk@parliament.wa.gov.au . Support How to search Hansard 2021 - current (41st and 42nd Parliaments) Hansard search Note: The 41st Parliament (2021-2024) is now included in these search results. Use keyword search for general words or phrases. Use quotation marks to search for an exact phrase. Use filters to refine your search. Parliament: select the four-year term of Parliament House: Legislative Council or Legislative Assembly Date range Member: Search by the member who spoke on a particular topic. Multiple members may be selected by pressing SHIFT when selecting a member from the dropdown list Bill: Find all search results on a particular bill Proceeding: Find all search results on a parliamentary proceeding, e.g. second reading, grievance, petition. Multiple proceedings may be selected by pressing SHIFT when selecting a proceeding from the dropdown list Select ‘Apply filter’ to run your search. Search results The default display order for search results is newest to oldest. Results can be further refined by selecting the metadata in the left-hand side of the screen. Electorate House Members Ministry Proceeding Subproceeding Parliament. Clicking ‘Download PDF’ in the top right-hand corner will download a print-ready version of the proceeding. Clicking 'Daily PDF' will download the full day Hansard currently available. Note, this document is generated from the online version which can be subject to further correction. See Hansard Publication below. Boolean operators The Hansard search requires all words in your query to appear in the result. So, if you search for maternity hospital , you'll only get results that contain both words. The Boolean operators AND, OR, and NOT only work as operators when your search terms are wrapped in double quotes. Without quotes, they're treated as ordinary search words. What you want How to search Example Either term (OR) "term1" OR "term2" "maternity" OR "hospital" Exclude a term (NOT) "term1" NOT "term2" "maternity" NOT "hospital" Both terms required (AND) "term1" AND "term2" "maternity" AND "hospital" Either term (alternative) term1 | term2 maternity | hospital Exact phrase "multi word phrase" "maternity hospital" What's NOT supported Proximity/numerical connectors for finding terms within a certain word distance are not available in the current search. Parliamentary debates August 2000 to November 2024 (35th to 41st Parliaments) Refined Hansard search (2000-2024) Use keyword search for general words or phrases. Use quotation marks to search for an exact phrase. Use filters to refine your search. Parliament: select the four-year term of Parliament (35th to 41st Parliaments only) House: Legislative Council or Legislative Assembly. You can also search for Assembly legislation committees or Assembly estimates. Member: Search by the member who spoke on a particular topic. Multiple members may be selected. Bill: Find all search results on a particular bill Committees: Search for references to standing committees in Parliament. Dates: Select a custom date search by Year Date Date range. Proceeding: Find all search results on a parliamentary proceeding, e.g. second reading, grievance, petition. Page no.: Search for a particular page in the final Hansard. Results per page: the default is 100 Sort order: Select the order in which you want your results displayed Search results Click on the date on the left side to bring up the PDF of that proceeding. Click on the PDF symbol on the right to access the Hansard of the entire day. Results can be further refined by adding more filters to the advanced search on the results page. Update: Hansard Search filters now apply to speeches for the 41st and 42nd Parliament (2021-current day). The Refined Hansard search (2000 - 2024) will remain available during this transition. Historical Hansard 1870 to July 2000 Hansard search Hansards between 1870 to 2000 have been scanned from the printed bound volumes and search results may not always be reliable. Use keyword search for general words or phrases. Use quotation marks to search for an exact phrase. Use filters to refine your search. Parliament: select the four-year term of Parliament House: Legislative Council or Legislative Assembly Date range Note : Filters for bills, proceedings and members will not work for Hansards prior to 2021. Select ‘Apply filter’ to run your search. Search results The default display order for search results is newest to oldest. The Hansard indexes provide information about member speeches and subjects, and can be used to assist your search. Find the indexes here: Hansard Indexes . For those who were familiar with the previous method of searching the 1870-2000 Hansards, the search is available here Frequently asked questions How can I find all the speeches made by a particular member? You can find all of a current member’s speeches in their member’s page on the Parliament website, by navigating to Current Members and searching or browsing for the member. Member speeches are separated into two categories: Speeches prior to 2021, returning refined Hansard search (2000 - 2024) results Speeches from 2021 onwards, returning results using the current Hansard Search . To search for speeches by former members, use the Refined Hansard search (2000-2024) , select the Member filter, and press Search. For members who served prior to 2000, use the Historical Search or the Hansard Search to free text search their name and/or topic. How can I read what was said on a bill? The Bills section of the public website displays a history on each bill page, a copy of the bill, the explanatory memorandum and a link to second reading speeches. To find further debates in the Hansard search, select the relevant bill from the dropdown list and select Search. How can I find the broadcast for a particular speech? Videos of parliamentary debates from April 2021 are available on our Video Archives . Why are there multiple Hansard searches? We are progressively upgrading the Hansard search to provide a more modern, consistent and powerful way to search parliamentary records. Hansard is the official record of parliamentary debates and a historically significant resource, and it is important that users can easily and reliably find information within Hansard. Because historical Hansard records have been created and stored in different formats over many years, upgrading the search is a complex process. Each Parliament must be carefully reviewed and prepared before it can be added to the new system. During this project, multiple search tools will remain available. How to find committee transcripts Committee transcripts are published in the committees section of the public website, for both current and past committees. When is Hansard available? Hansard is published progressively throughout the sitting day, with the full version generally appearing online within three hours of the house rising. This is a draft version, with the final, corrected Hansard appearing two to three days after the sitting. Finalised Hansard is available: for Tuesday by <TIME> Friday for Wednesday by <TIME> Monday following a sitting week for Thursday by <TIME> Tuesday following a sitting week. Please note: Public holidays may result in delays. Although we encourage the use of the Hansard record, the draft should not be quoted as it may be subject to further correction. Any changes made to the draft Hansard will be automatically reflected online. Support For assistance with Hansard or Broadcast, please reach out to the Reporting Services team on hansard@parliament.wa.gov.au For assistance with accessing and using parliamentary systems or using the public website, please reach out to itservicedesk@parliament.wa.gov.au or 08 9222 7200 .
